title: Ultrasound-Guided Sciatic and Saphenous Nerve Blocks En-hance Perioperative Analgesia in Sheep Undergoing Experi-mental Orthopaedic Hindlimb Surgery
content: The demand for refined anaesthetic protocols in ovine experimental surgery has increased due to ethical considerations and the need to improve perioperative stability. This study evaluated the analgesic efficacy of ultrasound-guided combined sciatic and saphenous nerve blocks using two different local anaesthetics in Hair Canarian Sheep undergoing invasive orthopaedic hindlimb surgery. Fifteen clinically healthy sheep were randomly assigned to one of three groups: lidocaine (2%), bupivacaine (0.5%), or control (general anaesthesia alone). Intraoperative physiological parameters, including heart rate, res-piratory rate, and arterial blood pressure, were recorded, and postoperative pain was assessed using a modified Melbourne Pain Scale. Sheep receiving locoregional anaes-thesia showed improved intraoperative physiological stability and significantly lower postoperative pain scores compared with control animals. The bupivacaine group ex-hibited the lowest and most stable heart and respiratory rates during surgery, as well as consistently lower pain scores during the early postoperative period. Lidocaine provided adequate intraoperative analgesia but showed a reduction in postoperative efficacy over time. Respiratory rate correlated more strongly with pain scores than other physiological parameters. In conclusion, ultrasound-guided sciatic and saphenous nerve blocks sig-nificantly enhance perioperative analgesia in sheep undergoing orthopaedic surgery. The use of bupivacaine resulted in superior and longer-lasting analgesia compared to lidocaine, supporting its inclusion in multimodal anaesthetic protocols to improve animal welfare and refinement in ovine experimental models.
